newsitem.title: USA: Lebanon monitoring group to discuss clashes.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon monitoring group to discuss clashes.

text.p: An international monitoring group is expected to meet this week to discuss fighting in southern Lebanon on Monday that killed at least nine civilians, the State Department said.

Lebanese militiamen led by pro-Israeli commander Antoine Lahd shelled Lebanon's southern port of Sidon after a roadside bomb blew up a car in which children of a late Lahd aide were traveling. Israel denied involvement.
"We think there will be a meeting of the monitoring group this week, which has been successful in the past in defusing these kind of situations," said State Department spokesman James Rubin.

The group of Lebanese, Israeli, Syrian, U.S. and French officials was set up in April 1996 after major fighting in southern Lebanon between Israeli forces and guerrillas of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah organization.
The fighting was ended by a U.S-brokered accord under which the rival parties agreed not to bombard civilians.
Rubin urged the combatants in Monday's clashes to return to last year's agreement. "We condemn these kind of attacks on civilians," he told a news briefing.
